items.title: Discover the problem
items.body: Understand the user, the workflow and the business need. Make assumptions visible and agree on the problem before discussing a feature list.

items.title: Define success
items.body: Agree on the outcome, the evidence we need and the constraints. Separate the goal from the solution so the team can compare different approaches.

items.title: Prioritize the scope
items.body: Weigh user value, business importance, effort and dependencies. Make the first release explicit, including what we are choosing to leave out.

items.title: Align the team
items.body: Turn the direction into requirements, flows and a prototype. Work through trade-offs with engineering and stakeholders before committing to delivery.

items.title: Support delivery
items.body: Keep decisions clear as the team builds. Review edge cases, acceptance criteria and readiness, and resolve questions with the people doing the work.

items.title: Learn and iterate
items.body: Use feedback and available product data to revisit the assumptions. Decide what to improve next and record what the team learned.
